subject: Azure co-sell: evidence scope & DPA alignment
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha.rao@contoso.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Azure co-sell: evidence we need for listing - quick scope question

Hi Asha,

Thanks again for the connect on the Azure co-sell path. Marketplace team asked us to bundle a short evidence packet so they can advance the listing and co-sell review. To avoid churn on the submission, can you confirm:

- Which of these artifacts you can share into the marketplace portal (sanitized): SOC 2 report (summary or bridge letter), a pen-test confirmation letter (sanitized OK), and an executed DPA that lists Contoso as the Platform buyer?
- Any required redaction rules for the pen-test letter (IPs, internal asset names, etc.)?
- For the DPA, should we name "Redwood Inference, Inc." as the "Service Provider" or the SRE/legal team prefers a different entity label?

We can supply a short cover note and sanitized SOC2 summary from our side. If easier, send the pen-test letter and DPA links and I’ll drop them into the marketplace submission.

Goal: get the listing to "security review passed" before our exec co-sell approval on 11/15.

Best,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Asha Rao <asha.rao@contoso.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Marketplace Procurement <procurement@contoso.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Azure co-sell: evidence we need for listing - quick scope question

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for laying this out. We can provide the following:

- A sanitized pen-test confirmation letter that states the engagement, scope high-level (web app + API layer), and a pass/mitigations summary. We will redact IP addresses and customer-specific asset names.
- A SOC 2 Type II summary bridge letter (latest period ended 2026-09-30). We cannot share the full report publicly; the summary and controls matrix are fine.
- A standard DPA in Docx/PDF; we will prepare a version with Contoso listed as the contracting party (buyer) and Redwood listed as the data processor.

Two notes:
1) The pen-test vendor requires a quick confidentiality acknowledgement (we usually add a one-paragraph NDA addendum for the full report; sanitized letter is OK for marketplace).
2) For the DPA, legal asked that "Redwood Inference, Inc." be used as the provider name — that matches our internal procurement records.

I’ll attach the sanitized letter and the DPA draft for your review. If you want the raw pen-test report, we can do that but it requires an internal request form and an NDA with the vendor.

Attaching: pen_test_letter_contoso_sanitized.pdf (PDF, 160KB); Redwood_DPA_v3.docx (DOCX, 48KB)

—Asha

Attachment: pen_test_letter_contoso_sanitized.pdf (PDF 160KB)
Attachment: Redwood_DPA_v3.docx (DOCX 48KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha.rao@contoso.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T08:29:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Azure co-sell: evidence we need for listing - quick scope question

Asha —

This is perfect, and thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple clarifying items so our security intake matches Azure Marketplace expectations:

- SOC2 summary: can the bridge letter include the period end date and the auditor name? Marketplace asks for those fields.
- Pen-test letter: we’ll need confirmation in the letter that the test covered any internet-facing endpoints for the service and that the vendor did not find any critical production vulnerabilities (a short sentence). Redactions of IPs are fine.
- DPA: good to confirm Redwood Inference, Inc. as provider. We’ll run the DPA through our legal team and route back any redlines; is Contoso comfortable with DocuSign for signature?

If that's all OK, I’ll upload the sanitized letter and DPA to the Azure portal and paste the HubSpot deal link in the submission so the marketplace reviewer can correlate the co-sell request.

Requesting one final small favor: can you add a single-line cover note on Contoso letterhead that authorizes sharing the sanitized pen-test letter with the marketplace review team? They like explicit authorization language.

Thanks — planning to submit this Friday 11/05.

Karthik

From: Asha Rao <asha.rao@contoso.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Marketplace Procurement <procurement@contoso.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T14:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Azure co-sell: evidence we need for listing - quick scope question

Karthik —

All good. Quick answers inline:

- SOC2: yes, the bridge letter will include auditor name (Brightline LLP) and reporting period (period ended 2026-09-30).
- Pen-test letter: vendor confirmed we can add the sentence you requested: "Testing covered internet-facing API and web portal; no critical production vulnerabilities were identified as of engagement report date." We'll keep IPs/hostnames redacted.
- DPA: procurement prefers DocuSign; I’ve generated the DocuSign envelope. Link below.

Also attached: Contoso_authorization_for_sharing.pdf — one-line authorization on letterhead.

DocuSign link (Redwood_DPA_v3): https://www.docusign.com/en/redwood/docusign/abc123
HubSpot deal for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/54892

If you upload these to the marketplace portal and send me the submission confirmation, procurement will mark this as "evidence delivered" and move the co-sell ticket to the next queue. If your legal has redlines on the DPA, we can accept them as comments in DocuSign before final signature.

Attachments: Contoso_authorization_for_sharing.pdf (PDF 2KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha.rao@contoso.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T16:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Azure co-sell: evidence scope & DPA alignment — uploaded and next steps

Asha —

Thanks — I uploaded the three items to the Azure Marketplace portal and linked the HubSpot deal. Submission ID: AM-2026-11-07-3327. I also dropped the sanitized pen-test letter and the Contoso authorization into our internal evidence drive for audit.

Next steps on our side:
- Lauren will watch for procurement signature in DocuSign and confirm when executed.
- Rishi will triage any follow-up questions from the marketplace security reviewer (likely about scope & mitigations).
- We’ll request a short co-sell kickoff with your GTM lead after the listing moves to "approved for co-sell".

Lauren, Rishi — please track this in the HubSpot deal and add the submission ID to the record.

Asha — can you confirm the expected turnaround for DocuSign signature? Procurement mentioned 3–5 business days but wanted to set expectations.

Appreciate the help here — will update the execs once we see the security queue move.

Best,
Karthik

Attachment: redwood_SOC2_summary_2026-09.pdf (PDF 320KB)
